claim_3.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed increased influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As expected, we observed strong, but highly variable, increases in influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells on day 7 (Figure 3A).

claim_5.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 1 post-vaccination (day 1), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that day 1 responses included innate immune-cell activation pathways including Interferon-related genes compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Overall, day 1 responses included pathways reflecting innate immune-cell activation, including Interferon-related genes, as observed by others (Bucasas et al., 2011; Nakaya et al., 2011; Obermoser et al., 2013) (Figure 3C and Table S3).

claim_6.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that adaptive pathways including Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress and N-glycan biosynthesis were more predominant compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: By day 7, adaptive pathways were more predominant, including those strongly associated with plasmablasts, such as “Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress” and “N-glycan biosynthesis” (see below) (Gass et al., 2004; Iwakoshi et al., 2003).

claim_8.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 1 post-vaccination (day 1) showed that CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes (ID65 and ID67), IFNα+ plasmacytoid DCs (ID78), activated CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, and both naïve and memory B cells changed coherently compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Again, day 1 changes reflected activation of innate immune cells, including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes (ID65 and ID67) and IFNa+ plasmacytoid DCs (ID78), populations that have been linked to vaccination efficacy and responses to influenza (Fonteneau et al., 2003; van Duin et al., 2007). However, we also observed changes in adaptive cell populations, particularly those reflecting activation of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, as well as both naïve and memory B cells (Kaminski et al., 2012).

sources.quote: Day 7 responses primarily reflected changes in adaptive cell populations, including plasmablasts (ID87) as expected, but also a related CD20+ B subset that expressed CD27 and CD38 (ID96, Figure S3), as well as activated T cell populations.

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_21.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), after removing age, gender, and ancestry effects by linear regression, showed that integrating pathway/transcript data with cell-population data predicted day 70 antibody-response endpoints less accurately than using cell populations alone.

sources.quote: Notably, predictive models could be built by using cell populations alone (Figure 6B)—integrating pathway/transcript with cell population data performed substantially worse (best median AUC was 0.6 vs. 0.78 using cell populations alone).

sources.quote: Only some of these populations, primarily the T cell subsets, contributed to the prediction of MFC (Figure 6C). Thus, by accounting for baseline serology using adjMFC, we uncovered additional baseline predictors.
